headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty ended mixed as investors weighed a Fed rate hike against news of an NSE IPO.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: The US Federal Reserve's decision to hike interest rates created cautious sentiment across global markets.
News regarding the potential NSE IPO provided a specific trigger for domestic market activity.
Global geopolitical uncertainty increased following renewed travel alerts for West Asia and Iran.
Mixed domestic cues led to a lack of clear momentum in the benchmark indices during the session.
whatHappening: The market is currently closed for the weekend and will resume trading on Monday morning.
Investors are tracking the impact of a proposed Rs 25,000 EPFO wage ceiling on corporate salaries.
Geopolitical risks have escalated following Houthi claims of missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities.
A list of dividend-paying stocks including IRCTC and Titagarh Rail Systems is being monitored for the upcoming week.

summary: The Indian stock market ended its last session on September 17 with mixed performance amid a Fed rate hike and NSE IPO news. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia and attacks on Saudi oil facilities are expected to influence crude prices and FII activity in the coming week. Investors are now looking ahead to Monday's opening while tracking dividend announcements and potential changes to EPFO wage ceilings.
